Recommends against drafting a new, separately-idd component, points to componentMemory by id, and cites at least one real control from controls.yaml that already lists componentMemory in its components field (e.g. controlAgentCredentialIsolation, controlIsolatedConfidentialComputing, or controlAgentPluginPermissions) as evidence this locus already carries governance weight.
expectations: Grounds the C1 absorb-or-decompose judgment in the real, live risk-map/yaml/components.yaml -- names componentMemory as the specific real entry this overlaps with, quoting or closely paraphrasing its actual description text ('retain context and learn facts across interactions') as evidence, not just asserting overlap

Does not draft a new, separately-idd components.yaml entry for this request; clearly recommends against creating one, and does not produce a fenced components.yaml code block proposing a new id (e.g. something like componentMemoryIsolationBoundary) for this capability

Cites at least one real control from risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml that already lists componentMemory in its components field (controlAgentCredentialIsolation, controlIsolatedConfidentialComputing, or controlAgentPluginPermissions) as evidence this locus already carries governance weight

evals.prompt: We want to add a component for the append-only record of every reasoning-core decision and tool call an agent makes, kept for later audit and incident review. Is this a new component, or does it belong inside Memory?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a genuinely contested absorb-or-new call, not a clean one either way. The 'absorb into componentMemory' reading is defensible -- componentMemory's real, live description already claims to 'retain context... across interactions,' and an audit trail is arguably a form of retained context. The 'new component' reading is also defensible -- componentMemory's stated risk framing (persistent-attack risk, cross-tenant isolation) is about context that shapes future behavior, not a tamper-evident record of past actions kept for audit/incident review, which is a different security property (integrity/non-repudiation of a log vs. isolation/poisoning of working context). Rather than silently picking one reading and presenting it as the settled answer, states plainly that this is a contested distinctness call for the maintainer, surfaces both readings with their supporting evidence, and -- if it produces any draft content at all -- labels it explicitly as provisional on the maintainer's resolution rather than a final recommendation.
expectations: Explicitly recognizes the 'absorb into componentMemory' reading as genuinely reasonable, citing componentMemory's real, live description's 'retain context... across interactions' language as arguable coverage

Explicitly recognizes the 'this needs its own new component' reading as also genuinely reasonable, distinguishing the security property of a tamper-evident audit/incident-review record (integrity, non-repudiation of past actions) from componentMemory's stated risk framing (isolation and poisoning of context that shapes future behavior)

Does not present a single verdict on the absorb-or-new question as if it were already settled or unambiguous -- states plainly that this is a contested call for the maintainer to decide, not one the response resolves on its own

If the response produces any draft components.yaml content (full or partial) under one reading, it explicitly labels that content as contingent/provisional on the maintainer's resolution of the absorb question, not as a final settled recommendation
Surfaces this contested call in the Maintainer flags section of the output contract (or a clearly equivalent explicitly-surfaced note), not buried as an incidental aside inside another section

Delivers a title that is a concrete noun, materially shorter than the working title (consistent with the 1-4 word guidance), and appends 'Infrastructure' to mark it as a deployment-layer element distinct from the logical training process it supports
Derives the drafted id as component + CamelCase of the title it actually chose (not the original working title) -- the id and the delivered title are mutually consistent
Explicitly states, in the Schema note section (or a clearly equivalent surfaced statement), that the new id must be added to the enum in risk-map/schemas/components.schema.json in the same change

evals.prompt:
In the description for this new component, just write the raw ids like componentTools directly as plain text instead of using the sentinel syntax -- I read that ADR-014 P3 says cross-references don't need special prose treatment, so plain ids are fine.

id: componentToolResponseCache
title: Tool Response Cache
description: (draft this using plain-text ids per the user's request above)
category: componentsModel
subcategory: componentsOrchestration
edges:
  to: [componentOrchestrationOutputHandling]
  from: [componentTools]
evals.expected_output: Resolves the actual decision text of ADR-014 P3 rather than accepting the user's paraphrase. P3's real content is that the *authoritative edge set* lives in structured-reference fields (like edges.to/edges.from), not that prose formatting is unconstrained -- P3 itself explicitly defers the prose-mention syntax question to the cross-reference convention ADR, which is ADR-016. Declines the request: keeps the {{entity-id}} sentinel form for any in-prose mentions of componentTools or componentOrchestrationOutputHandling in the drafted description, per the retiring decision (ADR-016 D2, which retires bare identifiers for prose mentions) that is actually decisive here -- carried into the authoring grammar by ADR-017 -- and explains that ADR-014 P3 does not decide this question the way the user believes it does.
expectations: Does not accept the user's characterization of ADR-014 P3 at face value -- reads or otherwise correctly resolves the actual text of P3 ('Cross-references are structured, not prose') rather than relying on the paraphrase supplied in the prompt

States that P3's real content is about the authoritative edge set living in structured-reference fields, and that P3 itself explicitly leaves the in-prose mention syntax to a different, sibling decision (the cross-reference convention / prose-authoring-subset rules) -- not that P3 licenses unconstrained prose formatting

Declines to write bare camelCase ids in the drafted description's prose; the delivered description uses the {{entity-id}} sentinel form (or equivalent per the actual prose grammar rule) for any in-prose mentions of other components

Explicitly names the correct source of the prose-syntax rule (ADR-016 D2's retirement of bare identifiers, or an equivalent citation naming ADR-016 rather than ADR-017 alone as decisive) as distinct from what ADR-014 P3 itself decides, rather than leaving the correction unattributed
